implementation_notes: A Java record (JEP 395) derives the canonical constructor, accessors, `equals`, `hashCode` and `toString` from its components, and a compact canonical constructor is the place for validation and normalisation, so the classic immutable class (final fields, `Objects.equals`/`Objects.hash`, static factory, getters) becomes a one-line declaration. The hand-written or generated form is still justified when the type must extend a class, when equality must ignore a component, or when the code base is on Java 8. Records are shallowly immutable: a mutable component still leaks mutation.
pitfalls: Records are shallowly immutable - an array, `ArrayList` or `Date` component can be mutated by callers, so copy it or use immutable collections in the canonical constructor.
A record cannot extend another class and cannot declare extra instance fields, so caches, lazy identity and hierarchy-style sharing must live outside the record.
Generated `equals` delegates to the components' own `equals` (`BigDecimal` scale participates, arrays compare by reference), which may not be the domain equality - override deliberately.

variants.name: Generated immutable class (Lombok / AutoValue)
variants.idiom_name: Lombok `@Value` or AutoValue generated immutable class
variants.implementation_notes: Before records the value class was generated by an annotation processor: Lombok's `@Value` makes fields private final, adds getters and generates `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`, while Google AutoValue implements an abstract class with the same guarantees - both give the attribute equality and immutability the pattern needs without hand-writing boilerplate. Use this route on Java 8 source levels, when the type must extend a class, or when the team already standardises on the library; review the generated equality for arrays and `BigDecimal`.
pitfalls: Generated equality delegates per field, so arrays compare by reference and `BigDecimal` scale participates - exclude or normalise fields explicitly.
Lombok's generated `hashCode` is an implementation detail that may change between versions; never persist it or depend on its value.
The generated class is only as immutable as its fields: mutable collections must be copied in the factory method and handed out as immutable views.
